thread:
maria: ok team — prototype for the 'stitcher' traffic generator is up, trying to capture sharp microbursts + heavy tail. want quick sanity checks :eyes:
aj: nice. what's the high level difference from the existing weavers/surge tools?
samir: main idea: stitch short high-qps bursts into slower ramps, then overlay long-tailed background to exercise KV coldness and kernel-switch churn. we call it 'burst-stitcher' rn.
jess: sounds promising. any config snippet? would like to run apples-to-apples vs replay harness.
maria: yup — sample config below (rough):
```
seed: 42
base_qps: 40
stitcher:
  bursts:
    - qps: 1200
      length_ms: 150
      cadence_ms: 5000
    - qps: 600
      length_ms: 300
      cadence_ms: 20000
  ramp_profile:
    type: 'cosine'
    duration_s: 600
tail_overlay:
  p95_rate: 0.02
  heavy_tail_alpha: 2.8
kv_warmup: true
batching_heuristics:
  max_batch_ms: 8
  backoff_threshold: 0.7
  dynamic_kernel_select: true
```
aj: handful of notes: (1) keep bursts short to hit kernel-switch in <200ms windows, (2) set kv_warmup=false when comparing against live replay to avoid confounding cache priming.
perf-bot: [deploy] burst-stitcher v0.1 deployed to perf-cluster-3 at 2026-03-18T14:12:09Z
oliver: when you say kernel-switch churn — you mean runtime switching between int8-optimized kernel and fp16 fallback based on seq len/batch shape, right?
samir: exactly. if our batcher collapses small requests into larger batches during bursts, the kernel chooser can flip. that flip is expensive and sometimes causes >15% latency tail regressions.
maria: current experiment aims to measure three axes: queueing latency, kv-hit-ratio drift, and kernel-transition-induced tail spikes.
jess: how are you measuring kernel transitions? logs? perf counters?
maria: both. we emit a lightweight event on selection with fields: selected_kernel, reason, batch_shape. tail sampler correlates those events with latency spikes. example log line: `kernel_select: gpu_int8 reason=batch_shape(16x128)`
aj: also include per-batch KV hit metric. coldness tends to increase batching variance and causes odd backpressure.
perf-bot: [metric] test-run #324: avg_qps=520, p99=412ms, kernel_flip_events=38, kv_hit=0.72
samir: initial run shows pattern: after ~45s of sustained stitch bursts, kv_hit drops ~8% and kernel_flip_events spike. hypothesis: background inference evicts prefix caches and burst-induced large batches cause different kernel path.
oliver: oh — eviction + batch growth. maybe our prefix KV TTL is too short for stitch pattern. what is TTL now?
maria: TTL=30s default. trying TTL=90s in next run. also toggling batching_heuristics.max_batch_ms 8->12 to reduce flips.
jess: make sure to run apples-to-apples: same model + same bs-quant profile, only change generator. we need baseline replay and then 3 variants: (A) stitcher default, (B) stitcher long-TTL, (C) stitcher slower batching.
aj: metric list to capture: cpu/gpu saturations, kernel_select_stream, batch_size_histogram, kv_hit_ratio_over_time, p50/p95/p99, tail-cause tags (kv_eviction vs kernel_flip).
maria: agreed. I've wired up a dashboard tile. plotting kernel_flip_events as stacked bars and overlaying kv_hit line.
perf-bot: [run-scheduled] apples-to-apples: replay vs stitcher scheduled for 2026-03-18T15:00Z cluster perf-3.
samir: one gotcha — the replay harness bundles prefixes differently; need to ensure we don't accidentally re-order request IDs which changes cache keys. keep deterministic ordering.
oliver: good call. also capture per-request prompt length distribution; longer prompts push us to different kernels even without batching.
jess: after runs, let's do diff profiling: sample hot kernels with nvprof and compare instructions/warp efficiency for flipped vs steady-state.
maria: plan: run 6x 10-minute experiments, collect traces, then open a short postmortem thread with actionable recs (increase TTL? change batching timeout? smarter kernel hysteresis?).
aj: small tactical idea — introduce a kernel-hysteresis window: once a kernel is chosen for a device, prefer it for next N batches unless latency degrades beyond threshold. might reduce flip churn.
samir: agree. could be implemented as a cheap state in batcher. low-risk experiment.
maria: ok i'll kick off runs, tagging results here. if anyone wants early access to generator binary: s3://perf-artifacts/burst-stitcher/v0.1/burst-stitcher.tar.gz
jess: thanks — will watch metrics and grab traces. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: [result] run #324 finished: diff vs replay: p99 +18%, kernel_flip +210%, kv_hit -8% — storing artifacts at s3://perf-artifacts/burst-stitcher/v0.1/run324/
maria: ugly numbers but precisely what we wanted to uncover. follow-ups: increase TTL, add hysteresis, and run a variant with batching_heuristics.max_batch_ms=12.
aj: i'll prototype hysteresis patch today. can we gate behind a feature flag?
maria: yes, flag: batcher.kernel_hysteresis=true (default false)
oliver: ping me when you have traces assembled; i'll run nvprof comparisons.
samir: also scheduling a quick sync after results, 30m, to decide rollout for next week.
maria: thanks everyone. will post final run summary + links in ~2h. :white_check_mark:
